rendered: In Fig. 2[1]a, the bacterium with the largest |ΔCD| for BA@L-HGNRs is P.aeruginosa[2]. A vision model read its L-probe bar at about 192 mdeg[3]. That value was estimated from the bar height, not printed in the figure. Its bar is the tallest in the panel, and the values fall in the order the species are plotted, ending with S. aureus as the smallest.[4]

source.caption: Fig. 2. Construction and performance evaluation of intrinsic chiral single-probe sensor array. (a) CD difference induce by seven kinds of bacteria with BA@L-HGNRs and BA@D-HGNRs; (b) Optical response of BA@L-HGNRs toward seven kinds of bacteria; (c) CD spectra of BA@L-HGNRs incubated with seven kinds of bacteria; (d) CD difference induced by seven kinds of bacteria; (e) LDA and (f) HCA for the differentiation of seven bacteria with BA@L-HGNRs; (g) LDA for the differentiation of seven bacteria using BA@L-HGNRs based on conventional colorimetric outputs; (h) LDA for the differentiation of seven bacteria using L-HGNRs.
